detailed_findings.finding: The proof correctly reduces to showing that each variable has a power in I, then concludes finite-dimensionality from the finitely many residue classes of monomials with bounded exponents.
The coefficient-basis argument proving J ∩ S = I is valid and avoids needing a separate flatness citation.
The proof explicitly uses Hilbert's Nullstellensatz without a declared/allowed citation.
The weighted grading and homogeneity assumptions are unused; this is not a mathematical problem since the proof establishes a stronger statement, but it may matter for formalization clarity.

feedback_for_solver: Keep the present strategy, but make the dependency explicit: either cite an allowed Nullstellensatz result or split off/prove the needed auxiliary fact that for J ⊂ kbar[x_1,...,x_d], if V(J) = {(0,...,0)}, then each coordinate x_i lies in sqrt(J), hence some power x_i^(N_i) lies in J. The rest of the proof, including the explicit argument that J ∩ S = I, is fine.
reason: The argument is mathematically complete and proves the stated lemma (indeed a slightly stronger version, since the homogeneity/weight hypotheses are not needed). The base-change step to T = kbar[x_1,...,x_d], the deduction x_i^{N_i} in J from V(J) = {0}, the explicit proof that J ∩ S = I, and the bounded-monomial spanning argument are all sound. However, the proof explicitly relies on Hilbert's Nullstellensatz without any declared or allowed citation, so the dependency side is not clean enough to route directly.
